主要内容: Commodity traders are reaping significant profits as prices for oil, copper, and battery metals surge. This trend is reminiscent of the commodity super-cycle of the early 2000s, when robust Chinese demand drove prices to record highs. Doug King, who established his hedge fund in 2004, capitalized on this period, with his Merchant Commodity Fund managing around $2 billion at its peak. However, the boom collapsed following the 2008 global financial crisis and the rise of U.S. shale production, leading to a sharp decline in prices and the withdrawal of institutional investors. The current surge in commodity prices is once again attracting substantial investment, highlighting the cyclical nature of these markets.
